incidente.resumo: An automatic Google Cloud Platform migration took the primary node of a highly available Redis cluster offline, triggering a known bug in how Discord's API instances handle Redis failover and degrading the API; a misconfigured edge caching rule and an overloaded Cassandra cluster added to the degradation. After the API recovered, nodes of other services misbehaved and failed in a cascading failure whose exact cause was not known, and Discord was restored through a full service restart, with service fully restored at 16:52 PDT.

descricao.texto: At 14:01 engineers were alerted to anomalies via real time metrics and monitoring.
trechos: 14:01 - Discord engineers are alerted to anomalies via our real time metrics and monitoring

gatilho.texto: At approximately 14:01, a Redis instance acting as the primary for a highly available cluster used by the API services was migrated automatically by Google's Cloud Platform, and the migration caused the node to incorrectly drop offline, forcing the cluster to rebalance.
trechos: At approximately 14:01, a Redis instance acting as the primary for a highly-available cluster used by our API services was migrated automatically by Google’s Cloud Platform.
This migration caused the node to incorrectly drop offline, forcing the cluster to rebalance and trigger known issues with the way our API instances handle Redis failover.

descricao.texto: The node failure triggered a known bug in the way the API instances handle Redis failover (already scheduled for fixing); some API instances did not properly handle the failover, and the bug caused the overall integrity of the API service to degrade heavily.
trechos: This migration caused the node to incorrectly drop offline, forcing the cluster to rebalance and trigger known issues with the way our API instances handle Redis failover.
14:03 - Engineers identify that some API instances are not properly handling the failover and begin investigation.
Despite this expectation, the node failure triggered a bug that we’ve known about for sometime, and something we’ve previously scheduled for fixing in the next few weeks.
This bug caused the overall integrity of our API service to degrade heavily, and uncovered a previously unknown cache misconfiguration which was resolved during the incident.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: A misconfigured edge caching rule for an expensive API route caused clients to aggressively call the route, degrading overall API performance.
trechos: A misconfigured edge caching rule for an expensive API route is discovered, causing clients to aggressively call this route, degrading overall API performance.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The number of requests to that API endpoint caused a non-critical Cassandra cluster to fall over under load, and the resulting Cassandra issues caused API latency.
trechos: Engineers discover that the number of requests to this API endpoint has caused a non-critical Cassandra cluster to fall over under load and begin working to fix it.
Engineers yet again execute a rolling restart of all API instances to resolve latency issues experienced due to the Cassandra cluster issues.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The initial failure caused some nodes of other services to behave incorrectly and eventually run out of memory and fail, triggering a cascading failure despite existing safeguards; during the incident a "guilds" node and then some "sessions" nodes were identified as misbehaving. The exact cause is not known, and a later update reports potential flaws in a library the service uses.
trechos: 15:46 - A node from the “guilds” cluster is identified to be misbehaving, causing a portion of all Discord’s “guilds” to appear offline for users.
15:55 - Engineers discover that some nodes from another cluster, the “sessions” cluster appear to be misbehaving, and being to investigate.
The exact cause of why this initial API partial outage cascaded into a full system failure is not known at this time.
We do know that the initial failure caused some nodes of other services to behave incorrectly, and eventually caused those nodes to run out of memory and fail.
These nodes triggered a cascading failure within the system, despite the various safeguards we have in place.
After investigation we discovered potential flaws with a library this service uses, and we’re currently working on rolling out an update we believe should resolve the problems.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: During the full restart, another component called "push" failed, and an important API setting for allowing users to quickly and safely reconnect was improperly set, which the authors attribute to human error.
trechos: 16:19 - Engineers are alerted to another system failure in a component called “push” and begin to attempt fixing through multiple methods;
Engineers realize that due to human error, an important API setting for allowing users to quickly and safely reconnect to Discord is improperly set.

passos.texto: Decided at 14:11 to execute a rolling restart of all API instances in an attempt to resolve Redis connection issues; the rolling restart completed at 14:15, but abnormal latency on API endpoints continued.
trechos: 14:11 - The decision is made to execute a rolling restart of all API instances in an attempt to resolve Redis connection issues.
14:15 - The rolling restart of API instances completes, and engineers inform our other teams that issues should be resolved.
14:16 - Engineers continue to observe abnormal latency on our API endpoints, and continue to investigate.

passos.texto: Between 14:18 and 14:57, corrected the misconfigured edge caching rule, disabled the problematic API endpoint on the upstream edge network, recovered the Cassandra cluster and executed another rolling restart of all API instances; at 14:57 the API returned to a nominal state.
trechos: Between 14:18 and 14:57:
The misconfiguration is corrected.
The API endpoint causing problems is disabled on our upstreams edge network, as its contents cannot be cached while the endpoint is unavailable.
The Cassandra cluster is recovered, and resumes normal service.
Engineers yet again execute a rolling restart of all API instances to resolve latency issues experienced due to the Cassandra cluster issues.
14:57 - All previous known issues are resolved and the API returns to a nominal state.

passos.texto: At 15:50 forcefully removed the misbehaving "guilds" node from the service's hashring, hoping it would decommission itself, and at 15:52 forcefully restarted the node, which succeeded.
trechos: 15:50 - Engineers forcefully remove the node from the services hashring, which they hope will force the server to properly decommission itself.
15:52 - Engineers decide to forcefully restart the misbehaving node, which succeeds.

passos.texto: Decided at 16:07 to institute a full service restart, forcing all users to reconnect and resetting the invalid state of various services; began rebooting components at 16:10.
trechos: 16:07 - Engineers decide that the best path forward is to institute a full service restart, forcing all users to reconnect and resetting the invalid state various services are experiencing.
16:10 - Engineers being the process of rebooting various components of Discord’s system.

passos.texto: After the "push" component failed, one engineer attempted to restore it while another began blacklisting traffic that relies on it to reduce load; between 16:20 and 16:32 the improperly set API reconnect setting was corrected.
trechos: 16:19 - Engineers are alerted to another system failure in a component called “push” and begin to attempt fixing through multiple methods;
One engineer begins to investigate the problems with the system, and attempt to restore service.
Another engineer begins to blacklist various pieces of traffic that rely on the system in an attempt to reduce load.
Between 16:20 and 16:32
This improperly configured API setting is corrected.

acoes.texto: Planned: fix the known issues with Redis failovers, whose priority has been increased, hoped within the coming weeks.
trechos: We’ve increased the priority of fixing the known issues with Redis failovers. We hope to accomplish this within the coming weeks to avoid further problems caused by individual node failures.

acoes.texto: Already done: modified the behavior of the improperly cached route to handle this type of error without degrading other services.
trechos: We've modified the behavior of the improperly cached route to handle this type of error properly in the future, without degrading other services.

acoes.texto: Already done: added monitoring around some of the signals that would have alerted the team to the cascading failure early enough to investigate and prepare.
trechos: We’ve added monitoring around some of the signals that would have alerted us to the cascading failure with enough time for engineers to investigate and prepare, possibly avoiding any issues altogether.

acoes.texto: In progress: rolling out an update to a library used by the affected service, after potential flaws were found in it, which the authors believe should resolve the problems.
trechos: After investigation we discovered potential flaws with a library this service uses, and we’re currently working on rolling out an update we believe should resolve the problems.

acoes.texto: Planned: improve the overall reliability and failure handling of the services affected by the outage.
trechos: We continue to plan for improving the overall reliability and failure handling of the services that were affected by this outage.
At approximately 14:01, a Redis instance acting as the primary for a highly-available cluster used by our API services was migrated automatically by Google’s Cloud Platform.
16:52 - Service is fully restored at this point.

perguntas_em_aberto: The exact cause of why the initial API partial outage cascaded into a full system failure is not known; the authors have theories and continue to investigate.
The authors are still not entirely sure why the flaws found in a library caused the cascading failures.

observacoes: Duration is computed from the approximate start at 14:01 to full restoration at 16:52 PDT; the API returned to a nominal state at 14:57 and a new anomaly was noticed at 15:41, so impact was not continuous over the whole interval. The date comes from the status updates posted Oct 13, 2017. The later update says the added alerts detected similar issues on a Saturday and a node was safely decommissioned.
